theorem: Section3 equation(3.1), Proposition3.1 and its proof
evidence: The plus Fermat quartic Jacobian is Q-isogenous to the cube of y²z=x³+xz². The first map is [-x³zy:x²z³:zxy³]; E103 divides its common xz factor, verifies the extension at every cusp, and derives the degree-four exact integral push–pull maps.
Each ideal class has an integral ideal of norm at most n!/n^n (4/pi)^s sqrt(abs(discriminant)). For Q(zeta8) the bound is24/pi²<3; the unique norm2 prime is generated by1-zeta8.
